sentences.text: This creature possessed a low skull measuring exactly 145 mm in length, and it lacked any head crest.
Its teeth were robust, sharp, pointed, and curved backwards.
The estimated wingspan of the type individual was 1.35 meters.
Haopterus had weakly built hindlimbs with metatarsals only 17 mm long.
Haopterus was the first Chinese pterosaur fossil to preserve a skull.
Researchers suggested that Haopterus moved quadrupedally on land and lived a piscivorous lifestyle as a specialized soarer.
Haopterus fossils date back 124.6 million years.
The genus Haopterus was named in 2001 by Wang Xiaolin and Lü Junchang.
The genus is based on holotype IVPP V11726, a crushed fossil discovered in 1998 at the Sihetun locality.
An analysis by Kellner et al. in 2019 showed Haopterus to be a close relative of Mimodactylus.
Haopterus and Mimodactylus form the family Mimodactylidae, which is the sister group to the Istiodactylidae.
Haopterus lived during the Barremian-Aptian age of the Lower Cretaceous in the Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China.
Haopterus lived between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
